summary.brief: Man mixes banana, yogurt and Nutella, freezes the blend in popsicle molds, and enjoys the treats with two children.
summary.detailed: The video opens with an adult man wearing a black shirt, glasses and a white chef’s hat, holding a toddler on his hip while a young girl in a bunny‑ear hat stands beside them in front of a white kitchen backdrop with a refrigerator. A cartoon title card appears, then the man lifts a spoon and two small popsicle sticks. He mashes a large overripe banana in a white bowl, adds about 500 ml of vanilla yogurt and mixes until incorporated, then stirs in two to four tablespoons of Nutella, creating a smooth, slightly marbled mixture. He pours the creamy blend into individual green‑handled popsicle molds and places the molds in a freezer to set. After the freezing period, the scene returns to the kitchen where the man, still wearing the chef’s hat, holds the baby and the two children each hold a frozen yogurt popsicle; they lick, smile and wave at the camera. The video ends with the Simple Cooking Channel logo displayed on a black background.

action.detailed: Mash the banana, blend it with yogurt and Nutella, stir until smooth, pour the mixture into popsicle molds, freeze until set, then enjoy the frozen treats.
action.actor: An adult man in a black shirt, glasses and a white chef’s hat, holding a toddler while preparing the popsicles

At the beginning of the video there is an image of the man holding two kids in one arm and the kids are wearing chef hats. To the right of the man is another kid in a white shirt with bunny ears on their head. To the left is a stainless steel refrigerator. The video is showing a cooking segment of a Channel called "The Simple Cooking Channel". The image alternates between the ingredients and the finished product. The smoothie is creamy and light, it has chocolate, as well as banana, and milk. There are other images of the finished product in the last shot which has six smoothies that are filled to just below the top in ice cube trays.

summary.brief: Man mixes mashed banana with yogurt and Nutella, then fills ice‑pop molds.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with an adult man in a black shirt holding a toddler while a young girl stands nearby; all three wear chef hats and wave at the camera as a title card appears. The camera then shows a close‑up of a white bowl containing mashed overripe banana. The man adds a white liquid from a measuring cup—yogurt—and stirs it into the banana until the mixture is smooth. He next drizzles a dark chocolate‑hazelnut spread (Nutella) over the blend and continues mixing until fully incorporated. Finally, he lifts the bowl and pours the creamy mixture into the cavities of a green plastic ice‑pop tray, filling several molds. The last shots display the tray with the partially and fully filled molds, ready to be frozen.

action.detailed: Combine mashed banana, yogurt, and Nutella in a bowl, stir until smooth, and then fill the ice‑pop molds with the resulting mixture.

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with an adult man wearing a black shirt, glasses and a white chef’s hat, holding a toddler on his hip while a young girl in a bunny‑ear hat stands beside them in front of a white kitchen backdrop with a refrigerator. A cartoon title card appears, then the man lifts a spoon and two small popsicle sticks. He mashes a large overripe banana in a white bowl, adds about 500 ml of vanilla yogurt and mixes until incorporated, then stirs in two to four tablespoons of Nutella, creating a smooth, slightly marbled mixture. He pours the creamy blend into individual green‑handled popsicle molds and places the molds in a freezer to set. After the freezing period, the scene returns to the kitchen where the man, still wearing the chef’s hat, holds the baby and the two children each hold a frozen yogurt popsicle; they lick, smile and wave at the camera. The video ends with the Simple Cooking Channel logo displayed on a black background.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
